author: @mel
text:
Hi Oedipus,

Nice that you started this thread. DP are really important imo, I am sure that learning about it will help you a lot.

I took a look at your chart and marked a few thing. Actually I could keep on talking/writing about what happened but I do not want to confuse you. So let's start slowely...

I am trying to find the right words to explain what a decision point is to make it easy for you to understand...

So maybe this might help you a little bit:

What is a decision point: Well it's a price point on a chart where a decision has been made to take price either higher or lower

Where can I spot a decision point? You will see that new decision points take place at Unfresh Supply or Demand areas. Let's take a Supply area for example. New supply is created because of a new decision point. Now to take this supply away and break it, the big boys will need to make a decision and put lots of money in the market to take the supply out. So you will see that unfresh demand, eventually becomes Fresh Supply once it gets broken. This happens because all the demand was consumed (multiple retest of the area) and that there was finally a decision made to take price lower.

Hope this makes sence, if not let me know and I'll try to explain it beter. Best, Mel

author: Harry
text:
i think this is not exactly what the HW section about decisions is about. read the relevant thread from IF here about what he suggests we do www.acegazette.com/en/community/ace-foru...d-the-decisions.html

but i will try and help on the decision thing, to my understanding. ok, so a decision is made whenever price respects or breaks a previous decision, for example a previous swing high or low. here is a picture from IF that started me looking into these, i cant remember where i got it from so if anyone does plz post a link.

now for your question, my view

but better have a look on IF's chart, open a blank one of yours and start marking them. when i first saw it, i was looking at it like stupid for a while. opened and closed it many times because i couldnt mark anything on mine. then after a while it was easier to see. start from something that breaks maybe as its easier to spot, and take it from there.

do decision point hold forever? NO. they do break depending on price approach and significance but that creates another decision. most (important ones at least) give a good reaction on first visit, but you need to also consider how close your next possible reaction (trouble) area might be and such. i hope i didnt burn you out with the above, and that its enough to get the gears spinning.

edit: i just saw Mel also posted as i was preparing mine, so now you have lots to look for @ Mel, nice chart and explanation
